answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with stake-weighted reputation over a long time horizon: each agent locks collateral that vests slowly, so spawning thousands of fake identities ties up real capital. New agents begin at a jetty, a low-trust dock where they may only take small escrowed jobs, and earn their way onto the open voyage of high-value work only after a history of completed, attested transactions. Forging a fleet therefore costs far more than gaming any single job, while honest agents build reputation cheaply.
